title: How to Choose a Forex Broker: What Actually Matters
excerpt: Regulation, spreads, execution model, and withdrawal speed — the real checklist before you deposit.
body:
Picking a broker isn't about who has the flashiest ads — it's about a handful of concrete things that decide whether your money is safe and your trades execute the way you expect.

## 1. Regulation

Check who actually regulates the broker — bodies like the FCA (UK), ASIC (Australia), or CySEC (Cyprus) carry real oversight. A broker registered only in an obscure offshore jurisdiction with no real enforcement is a red flag, no matter how good their spreads look.

## 2. Execution model

Brokers generally fall into a few categories:

- **A-Book** — your orders go to the real market; the broker earns from commissions/spread only.
- **B-Book** — the broker takes the other side of your trade internally.
- **STP / ECN** — orders route through liquidity providers, generally tighter spreads for active traders.

Neither model is automatically bad, but understanding which one you're using changes what to expect from execution speed and slippage.

## 3. Spreads and commissions

Compare the real cost per trade — spread plus commission — on the specific pairs you actually trade, not just their marketing headline numbers.

## 4. Withdrawal speed and reliability

This is where problem brokers show themselves. Look for real user reports on how fast (or not) withdrawals actually get processed.

## 5. Platform and tools

MetaTrader 4/5, cTrader, or a proprietary platform — make sure it supports the order types, charting, and automation you need.

None of this is financial advice — it's a starting checklist. Always verify a broker's current regulatory status directly before depositing funds.
